1: //! Bounded in-memory admission control for login attempts.
     2: //!
     3: //! # This runs *before* Argon2, and that ordering is the whole point
     4: //!
     5: //! Measured at ~300 ms per verification and 19 MiB (M002 closure), one worker
     6: //! thread can service roughly sixteen verifications inside the five-second reply
     7: //! deadline. Everything beyond that is already a `503`. A limiter placed *after*
     8: //! hashing would therefore let an attacker spend 300 ms of the appliance's CPU
     9: //! per request before anything refused it — which is a denial of service wearing
    10: //! a rate limit's clothes.
    11: //!
    12: //! So [`LoginLimiter::check`] is the first thing a login request does, before the
    13: //! command is admitted to the worker queue. `limiter_before_hashing` in
    14: //! `tests/authenticated_api.rs` proves the ordering by asserting that a
    15: //! saturated limiter produces `429` without any Argon2 work having occurred.
    16: //!
    17: //! # Shape: a token bucket with a bounded peer map
    18: //!
    19: //! Two independent limiters, because they defend against different things:
    20: //!
    21: //! * **Global** — caps the appliance's total verification rate. This is the one
    22: //!   that protects the worker thread, and it is what the ~300 ms figure sizes.
    23: //! * **Per transport peer** — stops one host from consuming the whole global
    24: //!   budget, which is what a distributed guess looks like from the listener's
    25: //!   point of view.
    26: //!
    27: //! The peer map is **bounded**. An unbounded map keyed by client address is a
    28: //! memory exhaustion vector all by itself: an attacker with many source
    29: //! addresses fills it and the process grows until it is killed. When the map is
    30: //! full the least-recently-touched entry is evicted, so the limiter degrades to
    31: //! approximately-global rather than to unbounded memory.
    32: //!
    33: //! # No persistent account lockout
    34: //!
    35: //! Counters live in memory and die with the process. A lockout persisted to disk
    36: //! would be a denial-of-service primitive: anyone who can reach the login form
    37: //! could permanently lock the operator out by guessing wrong a few times.
    38: 
    39: use std::{
    40:     collections::HashMap,
    41:     net::{IpAddr, SocketAddr},
    42:     sync::Mutex,
    43:     time::{Duration, Instant},
    44: };
    45: 
    46: /// The token-bucket shape used by both limiters.
    47: ///
    48: /// `Eq`/`PartialEq` are hand-written because the refill rate is an `f64`: a
    49: /// derived `Eq` does not exist, and a derived `PartialEq` would compare a
    50: /// double exactly, which two arithmetic-equivalent rates need not satisfy.
    51: /// Only tests compare these, and they compare the meaningful fields.
    52: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
    53: pub struct Bucket {
    54:     /// How much work is allowed in a full window.
    55:     pub capacity: u32,
    56:     /// How fast the bucket refills, as attempts per second.
    57:     pub refill_per_second: f64,
    58: }
    59: 
    60: impl Bucket {
    61:     /// Builds a bucket with a whole-number refill rate.
    62:     pub fn per_second(capacity: u32, refill_per_second: u32) -> Self {
    63:         Self {
    64:             capacity,
    65:             refill_per_second: refill_per_second as f64,
    66:         }
    67:     }
    68: 
    69:     /// Whether two buckets have the same shape.
    70:     pub fn same_shape(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
    71:         self.capacity == other.capacity
    72:             && (self.refill_per_second - other.refill_per_second).abs() < f64::EPSILON
    73:     }
    74: 
    75:     /// The smallest interval at which the bucket is fully refilled.
    76:     pub fn full_refill_interval(&self) -> Duration {
    77:         if self.refill_per_second <= 0.0 {
    78:             // A bucket that never refills is a permanent block, not a limiter.
    79:             // Callers construct these with a positive rate; this is the floor
    80:             // that keeps an arithmetic mistake from becoming a denial of service.
    81:             return Duration::from_secs(1);
    82:         }
    83:         Duration::from_secs_f64(self.capacity as f64 / self.refill_per_second)
    84:     }
    85: }
    86: 
    87: /// What the limiter decided about one attempt.
    88: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    89: pub enum Admission {
    90:     /// Allowed, and how much of the bucket is left.
    91:     Allowed { remaining: u32 },
    92:     /// Refused. `retry_after` is what the `Retry-After` header will carry.
    93:     Refused { retry_after_seconds: u64 },
    94: }
    95: 
    96: impl Admission {
    97:     /// Whether this attempt may proceed to Argon2.
    98:     pub fn is_allowed(&self) -> bool {
    99:         matches!(self, Self::Allowed { .. })
   100:     }
   101: }
   102: 
   103: /// One peer's bucket.
   104: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
   105: struct PeerBucket {
   106:     /// Fractional tokens available.
   107:     tokens: f64,
   108:     /// When this bucket was last used; drives eviction order.
   109:     last_seen: Instant,
   110: }

   114: /// Cheap to clone: every clone shares the same counters through a mutex, so

   117: pub struct LoginLimiter {
   118:     global: Bucket,
   119:     per_peer: Bucket,
   120:     max_peers: usize,
